title: Hero Party
body:
Goal: finish a family of hero classes (inheritance) and a Party that holds them (composition).

  1. Open starter.py in Thonny. Hero and Healer are done.
  2. Finish Builder, Explorer and Party.take_turn.
  3. Press Run. You should see:
Amara heals the team.
Kenji builds a bridge.
Sofia maps the cave.
Ravi cheers the team on.

Creative: invent your own hero class with its own power and action. Give your heroes names from many different places and cultures.

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Look at Healer. It is a finished example, and Builder and Explorer follow the same pattern. Compare the sentences in the README with the ones in the TODO comments. Spell them exactly the same.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: A child class sets itself up by calling super().__init__(...), which runs the parent's __init__. It can also define its own action method to replace the parent's. In take_turn, use a for loop over self.heroes and add each result to actions.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Each hero class needs two methods. The first looks like def __init__(self, name): and then super().__init__(name, "____"). The second is def action(self): and then return f"____". In take_turn, write for ____ in self.heroes: and then actions.append(____).

starter.name: starter.py
starter.html: # Hero Party - YOUR version # Inheritance: Healer, Builder and Explorer are all Heroes. # Composition: a Party HAS a list of heroes. # Finish the TODOs, then press Run and see if it does what the README says. class Hero: """Parent class for every hero.""" def __init__(self, name, power="courage"): self.name = name self.power = power def action(self): return f"{self.name} cheers the team on." class Healer(Hero): """(Already done - copy this pattern!)""" def __init__(self, name): super().__init__(name, "healing") def action(self): return f"{self.name} heals the team." class Builder(Hero): # TODO 1: __init__(self, name) that calls super().__init__(name, "building") # TODO 2: action(self) that returns f"{self.name} builds a bridge." pass class Explorer(Hero): # TODO 3: __init__ with power "exploring", and action() that returns # f"{self.name} maps the cave." pass class Party: """A group of heroes. The Party HAS heroes (composition).""" def __init__(self): self.heroes = [] def add(self, hero): self.heroes.append(hero) def take_turn(self): """Every hero acts once. Return the list of action sentences.""" actions = [] # TODO 4: loop over self.heroes and append hero.action() to actions return actions if __name__ == "__main__": party = Party() party.add(Healer("Amara")) party.add(Builder("Kenji")) party.add(Explorer("Sofia")) party.add(Hero("Ravi")) for sentence in party.take_turn(): print(sentence)
